messages:
monitoring-bot: ALERT: spike detected — correctable ECC errors rising on gpu-pool-eu-west1 (avg 32/hr across pool). link: https://grafana.internal/alerts/12345
Alex: seeing this on the dashboard now, thanks. Is this localized to specific racks/nodes? :eyes:
Marie: quick query I ran: `sum by(card_id)(increase(gpu_correctable_errors_total[15m]))` — shows 6 cards with >10 in last 15m, spread across rack-7 and rack-9.
Jamal: thanks. early thought: noisy cards but not yet causing XID fatals. What SLO impact are we seeing?
Ellen: latency SLOs for hosted inference haven't budged but error counts for a few tenants show elevated retries. I can pull per-tenant traces if needed.
Alex: priority: avoid user-visible failures. options: (1) manual isolate nodes, (2) auto flag cards for maintenance, (3) adjust scheduler to avoid affected GPU IDs.
Marie: propose a short runbook draft: detect -> cordon node -> migrate pods using `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` -> annotate card and create HW ticket -> if card correctables > 50/hr mark for replacement.
Jamal: prefer staged approach: first soft-isolate at card level (stop assigning new workloads to affected card ids) for 30m while continuing existing KV-cache sessions, then full node drain if errors persist. avoids thundering migrations.
Alex: can we implement soft-isolate via device-plugin labels? example: `kubectl label node gpu-node-42 gpu.avail=false` or set `node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable=true`?
Marie: device-plugin supports per-device attrs. we can add `--device-attr=quarantine=true` to our helper script and adapt the scheduler extender to respect it. POC would take a day.
Ellen: short-term automation idea: use alerting rule to create a maintenance annotation and trigger a pipeline that: 1) marks node as low-priority, 2) sets new allocations to other pools for 30m, 3) notifies infra oncall.
Jamal: suggested thresholds for automation (proposal): - soft-isolate: any card with >12 correctables in 15m OR >40 in 1h - escalated drain: any node where >2 cards hit soft-isolate within 30m OR presence of XID fatal in same window
Alex: rationale: short bursts should be absorbed (we batch and can move prefixes), sustained noise likely hardware. keep thresholds conservative to avoid churn.
Marie: here's the PromQL I used as a starting point: `card_spike = increase(gpu_correctable_errors_total{pool="eu-west"}[15m])` then `card_spike > 12` to flag. We'll also track `increase(gpu_uncorrectable_errors_total[1h])` to force immediate drain.
Ellen: logging snippet from one noisy card if useful:
```
[2026-03-10T04:12:03Z] gpu0: correctable ECC 14 in last 10m
[2026-03-10T04:15:10Z] driver: recovered from single-bit ECC, continuing
[2026-03-10T04:20:01Z] kubelet: workload retry detected, 3 retries in 5m
```
Jamal: ops playbook (short): 1) Confirm per-card metric (promQL) 2) Soft-isolate via device label 3) Observe 30m for escalation 4) If escalated, drain node and file RMA ticket 5) Postmortem tag with `gpu-failure` and hardware serials.
Alex: owners: implement alert rule and quiet window config — @Marie (lead) to own alert rule change; @Jamal to sketch device-plugin changes; @Ellen to add tracing dashboard to correlate tenant retries.
Marie: timeline: rule change and runbook doc by EOD tomorrow; POC device-plugin change by end of week. I'll open an infra PR with the PromQL and proposed thresholds.
ops-bot: Action created: infra#4567 - "Prometheus: add gpu correctable spike rule & annotation automation" assigned to Marie, due 2026-03-12.
Alex: one more operational note — cost tradeoff: frequent evacuations increase migration I/O and can push other nodes over memory thresholds. we'll add a rate limiter to automation to avoid >2 evacuations/hour per rack.
Jamal: agreed. add cooldown: `evac.cooldown = 1h` per rack. also add a manual override label `gpu.force-ignore=true` for tolerated maintenance windows.
Ellen: I'll prepare a short status note for all-hands next week summarizing the new thresholds and the impact model.
Alex: cool. if no objections, we'll proceed with this plan and iterate after a canary run on eu-west1-small pool. :thumbsup:
